note: Policy events and reporting changes on the timeline of APRA's series, each with its source. An event is context for a chart, not a cause: only an entry with an 'explains' field is claimed to explain a feature of a series, and only the April 2019 excess rule earns one. The report's chart markers and docs/findings.md are rendered from this file by etl/findings.py.

events.label: Lifetime Health Cover introduced
events.what: People taking out hospital cover after age 30 pay a 2% loading on the premium for each year over 30, up to 70%, removed after 10 years of continuous cover. Background: it predates the series, which starts in June 2007.
events.source_name: Department of Health and Aged Care, privatehealth.gov.au, Lifetime Health Cover

events.label: Medicare Levy Surcharge thresholds raised
events.what: The income threshold above which people without hospital cover pay the surcharge rose from $50,000 to $70,000 for singles and from $100,000 to $140,000 for families, from the 2008-09 income year.
events.source_name: Parliament of Australia, Tax Laws Amendment (Medicare Levy Surcharge Thresholds) Bill (No. 2) 2008

events.label: Private health insurance rebate means-tested
events.what: The rebate fell in three income tiers from $84,001 for singles and $168,001 for families, and stopped at $130,001 and $260,001.
events.source_name: Parliamentary Library, FlagPost on the legislation to means test the rebate (2011); National Seniors fact sheet on the enacted thresholds

events.label: Rebate tied to an indexed base premium
events.what: The rebate applies to a base premium indexed by the lesser of CPI and the insurer's premium rise, so the rebate's share of the premium falls when premiums rise faster than CPI.
events.source_name: Parliamentary Library, Bills Digest no. 35 2013-14 (Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Base Premium) Bill)

events.label: Private health insurance reforms
events.what: The maximum voluntary excess rose from $500 to $750 for singles and from $1,000 to $1,500 for couples and families; hospital products were classified Gold, Silver, Bronze or Basic, mandatory from 1 April 2020; insurers could offer people aged 18 to 29 a discount of 2% of the hospital premium for each year under 30, up to 10%.
events.source_name: Department of Health and Aged Care, privatehealth.gov.au, Private Health Insurance Changes
events.explains: The climb in hospital policies with an excess over $500 from this date: the rule allowed excesses above $500 for the first time (docs/series-breaks.md).

events.label: COVID-19: the April premium increase deferred
events.what: Private Healthcare Australia's member funds postponed the 1 April 2020 premium increase for at least six months.
events.source_name: Commonwealth Ombudsman, Private Health Insurance Quarterly Bulletin 94

reporting_changes.what: ACT figures were included with NSW until 30/09/2009 (APRA, Notes on Statistics); the ACT's population shows zero until then and NSW includes it.
An insurer reclassified its policies from non-exclusionary to exclusionary (APRA, Notes on Statistics).

unexplained.series: Hospital policies with an excess over $500 (single)
unexplained.what: A one-quarter step down with no note from APRA and no policy event found; the series is used from this quarter on.
The largest one-quarter move in the split, with no note from APRA; the split is never trended.
